claims.claim: Brin and Page's 1998 paper described a search engine that ranks pages using the link structure of the entire web (PageRank) rather than only page text.
claims.episode_span: Their 1998 paper described a system that would evaluate pages according to the structure of the entire web rather than the text on any single page.
claims.source_title: The Anatomy of a Large-Scale Hypertextual Web Search Engine (Brin & Page, Stanford)
claims.supporting_quote: it makes use of the link structure of the Web to calculate a quality ranking for each web page. This ranking is called PageRank

claims.claim: PageRank's treat-links-as-votes idea was borrowed from academic citation analysis.
claims.episode_span: treating links as votes of confidence, an idea borrowed from academic citation analysis
claims.source_title: The Anatomy of a Large-Scale Hypertextual Web Search Engine (Brin & Page, Stanford)
claims.supporting_quote: Academic citation literature has been applied to the web, largely by counting citations or backlinks to a given page. This gives some approximation of a page's importance or quality. PageRank extends this idea

claims.episode_span: Google launched as a Stanford research project in 1996 and incorporated in September 1998.
claims.supporting_quote: Brin and Page formally incorporated their company, Google , on September 4, 1998, in their friend Susan Wojcicki 's garage in Menlo Park, California

claims.claim: Page and Brin began the research project that became Google in 1996 as Stanford PhD students.
claims.episode_span: Page and Brin began the work in 1996 because existing search engines were failing under the web’s rapid growth.
claims.supporting_quote: Google has its origins in BackRub , a research project started in 1996 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin when they were both PhD students at Stanford University

claims.claim: Google's "Florida" update in November 2003 was the first major shake-up of its ranking algorithm, devaluing SEO spam tactics.
claims.episode_span: Google responded with successive updates—Florida in 2003, Panda in 2011, Penguin in 2012—each aimed at devaluing artificial signals.
claims.source_title: Google's Florida update: 20 years since the SEO 'volcanic eruption' - Search Engine Land
claims.supporting_quote: A couple of weeks earlier, the SEO community had witnessed the most major shake-up in Google’s ranking algorithm

claims.claim: Google Panda, introduced in February 2011, lowered rankings of low-quality content sites.
claims.episode_span: Google responded with successive updates—Florida in 2003, Panda in 2011, Penguin in 2012
claims.supporting_quote: Google Panda is an algorithm used by the Google search engine, introduced in February 2011. The main goal of this algorithm is to improve the quality of search results

claims.claim: Google Penguin, announced April 24, 2012, targeted sites that artificially manipulated link counts (link schemes).
claims.episode_span: Panda in 2011, Penguin in 2012—each aimed at devaluing artificial signals
claims.supporting_quote: for a Google algorithm update that was first announced on April 24, 2012. The update was aimed at decreasing search engine rankings of websites that violate Google's Webmaster Guidelines
